---
title: "Resources"
subtitle: "A small reference shelf — use the deck first"
---

Do not try to read everything below. The [lecture decks](slides.qmd) tell you what matters in a given week; these resources are dependable places to go deeper when you need another explanation, a derivation, or implementation context.

## Core references

| Use this for | Resource |
|---|---|
| One broad, modern textbook | Simon J. D. Prince, [*Understanding Deep Learning*](https://udlbook.github.io/udlbook/) |
| A rigorous second treatment | Christopher Bishop & Hugh Bishop, *Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts* |
| Hands-on PyTorch | [Dive into Deep Learning](https://d2l.ai/) |
| Classical reference | Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville, [*Deep Learning*](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/) |

## Video companions

- **Build from scratch:** Andrej Karpathy’s [Zero to Hero](https://karpathy.ai/zero-to-hero.html) is ideal for the early implementation thread and language-model construction.
- **Vision:** [CS231n](https://cs231n.stanford.edu/) is the most useful companion for CNNs, detection, and segmentation.
- **Language and Transformers:** [CS224N](https://web.stanford.edu/class/cs224n/) provides a deeper treatment of sequence models and attention.
- **Practical model work:** the [Hugging Face course](https://huggingface.co/learn) is the best bridge to modern tooling.

## Papers: read selectively

Read the original paper only after you understand the deck’s mechanism. The recurring landmarks are: ResNet, *Attention Is All You Need*, BERT/GPT, SimCLR/MAE/BYOL, VAE/GAN/DDPM, and FlashAttention. Individual deck endings name the relevant paper when it earns a close read.

## Interactives

[Interactive Articles](https://nipunbatra.github.io/interactive-articles/) hosts optional browser explainers for mechanics such as convolution, optimization, attention, contrastive learning, and diffusion. Follow the links on `[I]` lecture slides; they are the curated entry points rather than a separate parallel syllabus.

The course site also hosts small lecture-matched tools, including the Lecture 5
[EWMA + momentum explorer](interactives/ewma-explorer.html), which uses the same
seeded temperature observations and the same computed ravine as the deck and
notebook.

## For each lecture

1. Read the deck’s opening and its worked mechanism.
2. Use one notebook or interactive only if it resolves a concrete question.
3. Return to the relevant book or paper afterward, with the structure already in mind.
